# Spine: CLI-first application guide

> Create projects with Spine CLI, keep assembly in a reusable BuildApplication function, and verify the execution contract before running the app.

## Versions and sources

Use `go install github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli/cmd/spine@latest` for general installation and CLI upgrades. The current baseline is CLI v0.4.2 with the `platform-contracts-v0.6.5` recipe: Spine v0.6.5 and independent platform/validator v0.1.0 tags. Read the generated go.mod for actual selections. Check `spine version`, `spine schema --json`, and `spine capabilities --json`; source and tests are authoritative when prose differs. Go 1.25.5+ is required; playground apps require Go 1.26+.

- CLI source and full agent contract: https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli
- Framework API: https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine
- Echo HTTP implementation: https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-echo-platform
- Documentation map: /en/docs
- First app: /ko/learn/getting-started/first-app
- Project structure: /ko/learn/tutorial/1-project-structure
- Other languages use the same paths under `/en`, `/ja`, `/zh-Hans`, and `/zh-Hant`.

Use public packages; never import `github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/internal/...` from an application. HTTP apps use `spine.New(echoplatform.Option())` from `github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-echo-platform`; HTTP-less workers omit HTTP options and register event factories with `spine.WithEventAdapter`. HTTP alone does not add a WebSocket implementation.

## Documentation navigation

Top navigation separates Docs, Preview, Releases, Community, and Business support. Stable documentation shares a sidebar ordered as getting started, tutorial, core concepts, API reference, examples, and operations. Preview inputs and runtime OpenAPI use a separate sidebar. The version catalog, release channels, and release notes are under Releases; their existing /community URLs are preserved. The documentation map at /en/docs lists every localized page, including performance reports and support. Other locales use the same /docs path under their locale prefix.

## Release channels and publication

Channel selection and release process: /en/community/release-channels. Install stable CLI with `go install github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli/cmd/spine@latest`, Preview with `@preview`, or the current RC branch with `@rc`. These replace the same executable unless separate GOBIN directories are used. Branch names select branch commits, which may resolve to tags or pseudo-versions; branch existence does not prove a verified RC tag has been published.

Preview CLI uses `platform-contracts-preview` to resolve selected Spine modules at `@preview`. RC and stable use their own source recipes; installing CLI `@rc` does not automatically switch all app dependencies to `@rc`. Existing apps keep their recipe until explicitly changed. Check spine version, spine.toml, and go.mod.

Releases progress Preview → RC → Production through source CI, public consumer checks, maintainer approval, immutable tags, tag installation checks, and release manifests. Preview/RC use Actions artifacts; stable creates a GitHub Release. Core candidates are followed by six platform publications and completion of the full combination. CLI versions and schedules are independent. Current observation policy is 72h after verified Preview and 24h after verified RC; core stable releases also have a 168h interval, while CLI has no additional stable interval. These are minimum gates, not an automatic publication schedule. Pin published CLI tags and version the app source, go.mod, and go.sum together for reproducibility. Pinning the CLI does not freeze dynamic Preview dependency queries; new/update still resolve @preview.

## v0.7.0 Preview APIs

The stable instructions below target Spine v0.6.5. Install the latest Preview CLI branch with `@preview`:

```sh
go install github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli/cmd/spine@preview
spine version
```

Check the actual tag or pseudo-version with `spine version`. `@preview` selects the branch HEAD and may include changes between published tags. New projects use recipe `platform-contracts-preview`, resolving `@preview` for core and each selected platform or playground and recording canonical versions in go.mod. `--skip-install` still resolves these branches using Go and network access or module proxy cache; it skips installation and build checks. Existing versioned recipes stay pinned until explicitly changed. Preserve module, entrypoint, composition, port, layout, and implementation selections in spine.toml when changing recipe. Review `spine update --dry-run --json`, then apply with the matching `--if-match` hash. A changed resolution invalidates a reviewed plan. Go 1.25.5+ is required by core/Echo; playground requires Go 1.26+. General `@latest` installation remains the stable path.

Input DTOs and runtime OpenAPI JSON are available from core v0.7.0-preview.1. Embedded Swagger UI and ReDoc registration through `boot.OpenAPIOptions.UI` requires v0.7.0-preview.2. Resolve core and the selected HTTP platform together at @preview. HTTP v3, managed TLS, and the independent net/http platform first shipped with core v0.7.0-preview.3, Echo v0.2.0-preview.2, and net/http v0.1.0-preview.1. CLI v0.4.3-preview.4 supports --platform nethttp and HTTP v3 analysis. Current branch changes may be newer than published tags.

- Migration, exact version pins, and a complete application: /en/learn/migration/v0.7.0-preview
As verified on 2026-11-06, core 83b1e03 with net/http v0.1.0-preview.2 overwrites OpenAPI UI document and asset Content-Type with text/plain, so the documented UI example uses Echo v0.2.0-preview.3. HTTP status 200 alone does not establish browser rendering.

- Preview features, boot options, HTTP v3 migration, and merged fixes: /en/learn/migration/preview-features
- Runtime OpenAPI API: /en/reference/api/openapi

Declare separate pointer-to-struct parameters for body, path, query, and header sources. Use field tags such as `path:"user_id"`, `query:"page"`, and `header:"X-Request-ID"`, then read ordinary fields. Path tags match route keys by name, including case. Required fields follow the configured validator, not pointer-ness alone.

From v0.7.0-preview.1, query.Values/header.Values and their constructors and lookup APIs, query.Pagination, and path.Int/path.String/path.Boolean are Deprecated. Legacy-only signatures remain supported. In Preview, query.Pagination rejects repeated page or size keys with HTTP 400; single-value parse failures and missing values retain the existing defaults. Mixing any Deprecated input with new Path/Query/Header DTOs in one handler fails during boot even across different sources. Existing body DTOs and contexts may accompany either style, and separate handlers may migrate independently. No removal version has been announced.

New typed inputs reject invalid numbers with HTTP 400. Use pointer fields and apply defaults only when nil to distinguish missing values from zero. Query slices combine repeated keys and comma-separated values without trimming spaces or removing empty/duplicate elements. A missing path segment is not an optional DTO field. Ordinary non-pointer JSON values reject explicit null instead of becoming zero; missing fields, pointers, maps, slices, and custom JSON decoders have separate rules. HTTP v3 core parses JSON/XML/form/multipart without merging URL query or route parameters into bodies; Echo input Binder/JSONSerializer extensions no longer apply to Spine DTOs. MaxBodyBytes defaults to 32 MiB (negative disables); MultipartMemoryBytes defaults to a 32 MiB file budget (negative fails), not a total request memory cap. Uploaded files remain valid through AfterCompletion and are then cleaned up. PreparedApplication.Handler() is replaced by spine.NetHTTPHandler(prepared); external server shutdown and prepared.Close remain caller-owned. Managed HTTPS uses boot.HTTPOptions.TLS. Branch PR #34 adds per-role cleanup error history defaults of 32 entries/one hour and encoded-slash routing fixes; its v0.7.0-preview.5 candidate is not itself evidence of publication. Host fields read Request.Host.

Runtime OpenAPI 3.1.2 is opt-in through `boot.OpenAPIOptions{Enabled: true}` under HTTP options. The default path is /openapi.json, independent of GlobalPrefix. Path/Title/Version alone do not enable it. Without a validator, only route/method information and minimum OpenAPI placeholders are described. Detailed DTO inputs require a validator implementing SchemaDescriber. A validator without that interface can still describe legacy path wrapper types and Pagination page/size/defaults. Handler-selected response statuses remain under default; outside paths-only mode, described request bodies or parameters also add the framework 400 response for binding and validation errors. Legacy dynamic lookup keys, handler-local defaults, and runtime response status branches are not inferred. From v0.7.0-preview.2, import `github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/openapi/ui/swaggerui` and/or `github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/openapi/ui/redoc`, then add their `New(Options{})` results to `UI: []boot.OpenAPIUI{...}` with `Enabled: true`. The default UI paths are /docs and /redoc. Each UI accepts Path and Title; the schema URL follows OpenAPIOptions.Path. Selected UI assets and license notices are embedded with go:embed and served without a CDN. UIs remain opt-in, and their paths are independent of GlobalPrefix.

## Version catalog

Published tags, channel history, next target versions, and links to release notes and publication runs for the eight ecosystem repositories: /en/community/versions

A planned version is not a published tag. A core tag alone does not establish full platform cohort validation. Read the catalog check time and follow repository links for newer changes.

## Install, plan, and generate

The official installation package is `github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli/cmd/spine`; invoke the CLI as `spine`. To update the CLI itself, rerun the `go install` command below. `spine update` updates project dependencies and does not update the CLI executable.

```sh
go install github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli/cmd/spine@latest
spine version
spine schema --json
spine capabilities --json
spine new hello-spine --module example.com/hello-spine --dry-run --json
```

Read the `spine.cli-result/v1` envelope (`ok`, `exit_code`, `result`, `error`). Review `result.changes`, `result.diff`, and `result.base_hash`, then apply the same command using that hash:

```sh
spine new hello-spine --module example.com/hello-spine --if-match '<base_hash>' --json
cd hello-spine
spine context --root . --json
spine contract check --json
spine verify --json
spine dev
```

In another terminal, `curl http://localhost:8080/health` returns HTTP 200 and `{"status":"ok"}`. Stop the dev process before running another app on the same port.

Default `new` creates go.mod/go.sum, main.go, spine.toml, internal/application, src/controller/health_controller.go, and src/route/route.go. It installs dependencies, checks the static contract, and builds before publishing the project. It does not initialize the app, run tests, or open a listener. With `--skip-install`, run `go mod tidy` and `go mod download all` separately to prepare dependencies and all offline module metadata. Installed dry-runs may use the network and module cache. Use `GOWORK=off` when a parent workspace is active.

```toml
module = "example.com/hello-spine"
entrypoint = "."
composition = "./internal/application"
port = 8080
layout = "layered-v1"
platform = "echo"
recipe = "platform-contracts-v0.6.5"
websocket_platform = "none"
validator = "none"
```

The CLI also supports `event_platforms = ["events:kafka"]` for named event selections. These configuration keys describe generation and implementation selection; they are not broker credentials. Keep DB, broker, and authentication settings in application code or environment variables.

If static inspection reports `MODULE_GRAPH_UNAVAILABLE` after a manual dependency change, prepare the full module metadata before retrying:

```sh
go mod tidy
go mod download all
spine contract check --json
spine verify --json
```

## Platform selection and DTO validation

The core uses only the standard library. Public contracts are `contract/http`, `contract/websocket`, `contract/event`, and `contract/validator`. In v0.6.5, older `adapter`, `adapter/http`, `adapter/event`, and `wsadapter` paths remain compatibility aliases.

```sh
spine new chat-app --module example.com/chat-app --websocket-platform gorilla
spine new worker --module example.com/worker --platform none --event-platform events:kafka
spine new validated-app --module example.com/validated-app --validator playground
```

Select `--platform echo|none`, `--websocket-platform none|gorilla`, repeatable `--event-platform [name:]kafka|rabbitmq`, and `--validator none|playground`. Gorilla requires Echo HTTP; `none` HTTP requires an event platform. Review each command with `--dry-run --json`, then apply the same arguments with `--if-match` and the reviewed base hash. Configure broker environment variables according to the generated README. An `events` factory uses the `SPINE_EVENTS_` prefix. Generation installs selected modules and checks static contracts/builds; it does not execute factories or contact brokers.

In BuildApplication, create factories and validators first and check their errors. Compose `spine.New(echoplatform.Option(), gorillaplatform.Option(), spine.WithEventAdapter("events", factory), spine.WithValidator(validator))` with only the required options. Concrete modules are `spine-echo-platform`, `spine-gorilla-platform`, `spine-kafka-platform`, `spine-rabbitmq-platform`, and `spine-validator-playground`.

Create the optional validator with `playground.New()` and register it with `spine.WithValidator`. Bound HTTP JSON/form DTOs and decoded WebSocket/consumer message DTOs are validated before handlers. Without it, `validate` tags are not checked automatically. Rule failures produce HTTP 400 with `message`/`fields`, WS close 1008, or consumer NACK policy; validator execution failures produce HTTP 500 or WS 1011. `fields[].field` uses JSON Pointer and rejected values are not exposed automatically. Explicit nil validators fail preflight.

CLI upgrades rerun `go install ...@latest`. `spine update` updates project dependencies for the selected recipe only; it does not rewrite source, switch implementation choices, or automatically move an existing recipe. Migrate existing assembly/configuration manually, then review an update dry-run and apply with its base hash. Kafka/RabbitMQ boot options were removed in v0.6.5.

For an existing v0.6.0 app with no recipe, upgrading the CLI alone keeps `echo-v0.1.0-spine-v0.6.0` targets. Explicitly change or add the following selection keys in spine.toml while preserving module, entrypoint, composition, port, and layout. This example selects HTTP only; match websocket_platform, validator, and event_platforms to the actual assembly when selecting other implementations.

```toml
recipe = "platform-contracts-v0.6.5"
websocket_platform = "none"
validator = "none"
event_platforms = []
```

Then migrate application assembly/source, run `spine update --dry-run --json`, review changes/diff/base_hash, and apply the same command with `--if-match` and that hash. Check the resolved go.mod and run contract check/verify. Changing recipe/configuration after a dry-run requires a new plan and hash.

## Extend the generated project

Default `layered-v1` generators use database/domain, src/dto, src/repository, src/service, src/controller, and src/route. A resource composes role generators and does not implement a business handler or add a route automatically. Implement the handler, then register it with `spine g route get-users --method GET --path /users --handler src/controller:UserController.Get`. Review each generator plan with `--dry-run --json` and apply it with that plan's `--if-match` hash.

The site's feature-based `src/user` tutorials explicitly use a separate `legacy` layout, supported by the CLI with versions selected by its bundled recipe. They do not describe default `new` output. Start those examples in a fresh directory:

```sh
spine new my-app --layout legacy --module example.com/my-app --dry-run --json
spine new my-app --layout legacy --module example.com/my-app --if-match '<base_hash>' --json
cd my-app
spine generate resource user --dry-run --json
spine generate resource user --if-match '<base_hash>' --json
spine contract check --json
spine verify --json
spine explain http GET /user/:id
spine contract export --format openapi --output openapi.json
spine contract export --format asyncapi --output asyncapi.json
spine contract snapshot
spine contract diff
```

Use a separate fresh base_hash for each matching command pair. The legacy resource generates src/user/user_route.go, user_repository.go, user_service.go, and user_controller.go, registers user.Register(app), and provides GET /user/:id. Legacy slice --storage memory is development-only. Consumer and WebSocket skeletons return not-implemented errors until implemented. Kafka and RabbitMQ factory/configuration code can be selected by `new`; broker provisioning, Bun persistence, authentication, and outbox still require application decisions.

Keep main.go as BuildApplication → Validate → Run, and keep registrations direct and unconditional. Read analysis_complete and diagnostics; do not treat inspect as a validation gate. Never duplicate generated registration calls.

## Verification boundaries

- contract check validates static source; verify adds formatting, vet, and local tests.
- contract probe executes BuildApplication and Validate and reconciles only public consumer/WebSocket registries, not HTTP routes, DI, or interceptors.
- doctor is offline; DB, broker, authentication, listener, and deployed behavior need separate integration/E2E evidence.
- Arbitrary dynamic registrations remain unsupported. The CLI recognizes supported direct os.Getenv inputs; use the same inputs during inspection and runtime.

The runtime notes below use Spine v0.6.5. Full inline HealthController examples use the explicit legacy layout; the default layered layout keeps health code under src/controller and src/route. Historical external demo snapshots are labeled separately.

## Mental model

Application assembly is explicit:

```text
constructors + routes + interceptors + transport registrations
                         |
                         v
                  App.Validate(options)
                         |
                         v
        Run / RunContext repeats static preflight
                         |
                         v
       DI warm-up + registered read-consumer readiness
                         |
                         v
         consumers/custom transports, then HTTP listener
```

For Spine `v0.6.5`, which the CLI-generated project pins, a successful HTTP request follows this framework-controlled order:

```text
global PreHandle
  -> route selection
  -> argument resolution
  -> route PreHandle
  -> controller method
  -> response preparation and validation
  -> queued domain-event dispatch
  -> PostHandle in reverse order
  -> BeforeResponse in reverse order
  -> transport write
  -> AfterCompletion in reverse order
```

A failure before event dispatch skips the remaining success stages; eligible `BeforeResponse` callbacks, error rendering, transport write, and `AfterCompletion` finish the failure path. A later `BeforeResponse` failure can replace the staged success response, but it cannot undo events already dispatched.

Global `PreHandle` runs before route selection and receives empty `HandlerMeta`. In `v0.6.5`, body, multipart, and path argument resolution runs before route `PreHandle`; malformed input can therefore fail before route-level authentication executes. Use an HTTP-scoped global interceptor for authentication or rejection that must happen before binding, and route interceptors for route-specific checks after binding. Global checks cannot depend on resolved route metadata.

## Non-negotiable rules

- Register every DI-created controller, consumer, repository, service, and interceptor constructor with `app.Constructor`.
- A constructor is a function that returns exactly one value. It cannot return `(T, error)`, and neither the constructor nor its returned pointer may be nil.
- Register handlers as pointer method expressions such as `(*UserController).Get`, never as bound methods such as `controller.Get`.
- Check errors from `WebSocket().Register`, `Consumers().Register`, `Validate`, `Run`, and `RunContext`.
- Enable HTTP explicitly with `HTTP: &boot.HTTPOptions{}`. `HTTP: nil` means no HTTP server.
- Return `httpx.Response[T]`, `httpx.Binary`, or `httpx.Redirect` for successful HTTP responses. Do not return a raw DTO or raw string.
- Use `httperr.*` or `*httperr.HTTPError` for expected HTTP failures. Generic errors become a non-leaking HTTP 500.
- Use Spine semantic input types. Do not replace `path.Int`, `path.String`, or `path.Boolean` with primitive handler arguments.
- Keep Kafka/RabbitMQ consumers idempotent. Delivery is at least once, not exactly once.
- Use an outbox when a database write and external event publication must form one durable business operation.
- Never enable plaintext broker compatibility in production.

## Generated HTTP application

`internal/application/application.go`:

```go
package application

import (
	"os"

	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine"
    echoplatform "github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-echo-platform"
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/boot"
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/httpx"
)

type HealthController struct{}

func NewHealthController() *HealthController { return &HealthController{} }

func (c *HealthController) Get() httpx.Response[map[string]string] {
	return httpx.Response[map[string]string]{Body: map[string]string{"status": "ok"}}
}

// BuildApplication은 서버 실행, 계약 검사와 오프라인 검증이 함께 사용하는 composition root입니다.
func BuildApplication() (spine.App, boot.Options, error) {
	app := spine.New(echoplatform.Option())
	app.Constructor(NewHealthController)
	app.Route("GET", "/health", (*HealthController).Get)

	address := ":8080"
	if port := os.Getenv("SPINE_PORT"); port != "" {
		address = ":" + port
	}
	return app, boot.Options{Address: address, HTTP: &boot.HTTPOptions{}}, nil
}
```

Root `main.go` stays:

```go
package main

import (
	"log"

	"example.com/hello-spine/internal/application"
)

func main() {
	app, options, err := application.BuildApplication()
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := app.Validate(options); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := app.Run(options); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

Use `spine dev` to run it and `curl http://localhost:8080/health` in another terminal to check the response.

Use `RunContext(ctx, opts)` instead of `Run(opts)` when a test or service host owns cancellation. `Run` and `RunContext` perform the same static validation as `Validate`; calling `Validate` separately is still useful in CI and deployment preflight.

When validation returns `*boot.ConfigError`, inspect `Issues` and use each issue's `Code` as the stable machine-readable value. Do not parse the human-readable message.

```go
var configErr *boot.ConfigError
if errors.As(err, &configErr) {
	for _, issue := range configErr.Issues {
		log.Printf("%s [%s]: %s", issue.Path, issue.Code, issue.Message)
	}
}
```

`Validate` checks supported static options and registrations without network access. DI construction and registered consumer reader readiness occur later in `Run`/`RunContext`, before the HTTP listener is opened. Kafka publisher-only startup does not connect to the broker; actual publication is required to verify connectivity and delivery.

## Dependency injection

Dependencies are constructor parameters. For example, `NewUserController(service *UserService)` depends on `NewUserService(repo UserRepository)`, which depends on a single registered concrete repository implementing that interface. Register the whole chain with `app.Constructor(NewBunDB, NewUserRepository, NewUserService, NewUserController)`. Providers are lazy singletons and controllers/consumers are warmed up before traffic starts.

DI details agents commonly miss:

- A concrete provider can satisfy one implemented interface automatically.
- Resolving that provider through its concrete type and interface returns the same singleton.
- If multiple registered concrete providers implement the same requested interface, resolution fails as ambiguous.
- Circular dependencies fail with an explicit dependency path.
- A constructor panic is converted to a startup error.
- Direct interceptor instances do not need constructor registration. DI-resolved interceptors do.
- A typed nil interceptor such as `(*TxInterceptor)(nil)` is a type token asking the container for that type. Register its constructor first.

Example:

```go
app.Constructor(NewTxInterceptor)
app.InterceptorFor(
	boot.InterceptorHTTP,
	(*TxInterceptor)(nil),
)
```

## HTTP routing and method signatures

Register a route with:

```go
app.Route("GET", "/users/:user_id", (*UserController).Get)
```

HTTP methods are trimmed and uppercased. Route paths use `:name` parameters. Path semantic arguments consume path parameters from left to right, not by Go parameter name:

```go
app.Route("GET", "/orgs/:org_id/users/:user_id", (*UserController).Get)

func (c *UserController) Get(orgID path.Int, userID path.Int) httpx.Response[User] {
	// orgID binds :org_id; userID binds :user_id.
}
```

Static and parameter routes that overlap for the same method are rejected as ambiguous during boot. A global prefix must be static, start with `/`, and contain neither `:` nor `*`.

```go
HTTP: &boot.HTTPOptions{GlobalPrefix: "/api/v1"}
```

Use `route.WithInterceptors` for route-only policies:

```go
app.Route(
	"POST",
	"/admin/users",
	(*AdminController).Create,
	route.WithInterceptors(&AdminAuthInterceptor{}),
)
```

### Stable v0.6.5 HTTP inputs

| Handler parameter | Value supplied by Spine | Important rule |
|---|---|---|
| `context.Context` | Request context plus request-scoped event publisher | Use this with `publish.Event` and database calls. |
| `path.Int` | Parsed `int64` from the next `:segment` | Read `.Value`; invalid numeric values return HTTP 400 in v0.6.5. |
| `path.String` | Raw string from the next `:segment` | Read `.Value`. |
| `path.Boolean` | Parsed boolean from the next `:segment` | Accepts true/false forms supported by Spine; invalid boolean values return HTTP 400 in v0.6.5. |
| `query.Values` | All query values | `Int(key, default)` falls back on missing or invalid input; validate business ranges yourself. |
| `query.Pagination` | `page` and `size` | Defaults to page 1 and size 20; validate non-positive or excessive values yourself. |
| `header.Values` | HTTP headers | Use `Get` and `Has`. |
| `*SomeDTO` with no `form` tags | Bound request DTO | HTTP DTOs must be pointers to structs; the Echo binder and request `Content-Type` select the body format. Malformed JSON returns HTTP 400; unsupported body Content-Type returns 415. |
| `*SomeForm` with at least one `form` tag | Bound form DTO | The presence of a form tag selects form binding. |
| `multipart.UploadedFiles` | Uploaded file descriptors | Call each file's `Open` and close the returned stream. |
| `pkg/spine.Ctx` or `core.ControllerContext` | Read-only view of values set by interceptors | Only `Get` is exposed; custom interfaces with extra methods are unsupported. |

Arbitrary primitive parameters and application service parameters are not controller arguments. Put services on the controller through constructor injection.

### Supported HTTP outputs

| Return value | Result |
|---|---|
| `httpx.Response[T]` or `*httpx.Response[T]` | JSON for non-string `T`; plain text for string `T`; default status 200. |
| `httpx.Binary` or `*httpx.Binary` | Byte response with explicit content type; default status 200. |
| `httpx.Redirect` or `*httpx.Redirect` | `Location` response; default status 302. |
| `error` | Expected `httperr.HTTPError` or sanitized HTTP 500. |
| `(supportedResponse, error)` | Response on nil error; error response otherwise. |

`httpx.ResponseOptions` controls status, headers, and cookies:

```go
return httpx.Response[User]{
	Body: user,
	Options: httpx.ResponseOptions{
		Status:  http.StatusCreated,
		Headers: map[string]string{"Location": fmt.Sprintf("/users/%d", user.ID)},
		Cookies: []httpx.Cookie{{
			Name:     "session",
			Value:    httpx.EncodeCookieValue(token),
			Path:     "/",
			HttpOnly: true,
			Secure:   true,
			SameSite: httpx.SameSiteLax,
		}},
	},
}, nil
```

Spine validates status, JSON serialization, and cookies before `BeforeResponse`. Invalid cookie names, values, `SameSite`, or `Priority` fail without partially committing a success response. Use `httpx.EncodeCookieValue`/`DecodeCookieValue` for arbitrary Unicode or delimiter-containing values.

### HTTP errors

Built-in helpers are:

```go
httperr.BadRequest("...")
httperr.Unauthorized("...")
httperr.NotFound("...")
httperr.InternalServerError("...")
```

Use `*httperr.HTTPError` for another status:

```go
return httpx.Response[User]{}, &httperr.HTTPError{
	Status:  http.StatusConflict,
	Message: "email already exists",
	Cause:   err,
}
```

Expected errors serialize as `{"message":"..."}`. Generic errors return status 500 and `{"message":"Internal server error"}`; their original text is not exposed to clients.

## Interceptors

Every `core.Interceptor` must implement all four methods:

```go
type Interceptor interface {
	PreHandle(ctx core.ExecutionContext, meta core.HandlerMeta) error
	PostHandle(ctx core.ExecutionContext, meta core.HandlerMeta)
	BeforeResponse(ctx core.ExecutionContext, meta core.HandlerMeta, executionErr error) error
	AfterCompletion(ctx core.ExecutionContext, meta core.HandlerMeta, err error)
}
```

- `app.Interceptor(x)` applies `x` to HTTP and WebSocket messages.
- `app.InterceptorFor(boot.InterceptorHTTP, x)` applies only to HTTP.
- `app.InterceptorFor(boot.InterceptorWebSocket, x)` applies only to WebSocket messages and handshake auth when implemented.
- `boot.InterceptorAll` means HTTP plus WebSocket, not Kafka/RabbitMQ consumers.
- `route.WithInterceptors` applies only to that HTTP route.
- Reusing the same interceptor pointer across scopes merges its scopes and executes that instance once. Different instances of the same type execute independently.

For CORS, prefer startup validation and scope it to HTTP:

```go
corsInterceptor, err := cors.NewValidated(cors.Config{
	AllowOrigins:     []string{"https://app.example.com"},
	AllowMethods:     []string{"GET", "POST", "OPTIONS"},
	AllowHeaders:     []string{"Authorization", "Content-Type"},
	AllowCredentials: true,
})
if err != nil {
	return nil, boot.Options{}, err
}
app.InterceptorFor(boot.InterceptorHTTP, corsInterceptor)
```

Credentialed CORS cannot use wildcard origin `*`.

### Request transaction pattern

The Bun demo uses this safe boundary:

1. `PreHandle` begins a transaction and stores `bun.Tx` in `ExecutionContext`.
2. The controller reads it through `pkg/spine.Ctx.Get("tx")` and passes it as `bun.IDB` to the service/repository.
3. `BeforeResponse` rolls back when `executionErr != nil`; otherwise it commits.

Response serialization, cookie validation, event dispatch, and post-processing happen before `BeforeResponse`, so their framework-controlled failures can trigger rollback. This also means a broker event can be published before the transaction commit, and a later commit failure cannot recall it. A database commit is atomic with neither broker publication nor the physical socket write. Use an outbox for database-plus-broker atomicity.

## Swagger and transport extensions

From v0.7.0-preview.1, core can generate and serve runtime OpenAPI when explicitly enabled; see /en/reference/api/openapi. For stable v0.6.5, export the static HTTP contract with `spine contract export --format openapi --output openapi.json`. To mount Swagger UI in v0.6.5, import native Echo v5 and construct the app with `spine.New(echoplatform.Option(echoplatform.WithEcho(func(e *echo.Echo) { e.GET("/swagger/*", echo.WrapHandler(httpSwagger.WrapHandler)) })))`. Preserve the following constructor and route registrations. Native Echo routes bypass Spine interceptors and staging. The historical Bun demo snapshot below uses the removed App.Transport hook; use typed WithEcho for current code.

Use `App.RegisterTransport` only for an independent custom transport implementing `core.CustomTransport` (`Init`, `Start`, and `Stop`).

## WebSocket

Select the independent Gorilla implementation first (`--websocket-platform gorilla` or `spine.New(echoplatform.Option(), gorillaplatform.Option())`). HTTP upgrade support, a WS factory, and non-nil boot HTTP options are required. Register handlers with method expressions and check the registration error:

```go
app.Constructor(NewChatController)
if err := app.WebSocket().Register(
	"/ws/chat",
	(*ChatController).OnMessage,
); err != nil {
	return nil, boot.Options{}, err
}
```

Supported WebSocket handler inputs are:

- `context.Context`
- `ws.ConnectionID`
- raw `[]byte`
- a non-pointer struct decoded from the JSON message

Prefer `func (c *ChatController) OnMessage(ctx context.Context, id ws.ConnectionID, command ChatCommand) error`. Use `ws.Send(ctx, ws.TextMessage, encoded)` for the current connection. A non-nil handler error closes with WebSocket code 1011; DTO validation rule failures close with 1008; to keep the socket open for invalid application input, send a typed error event and return nil.

`ws.Send` sends only to the current connection. For broadcast or rooms, obtain `ws.Sender` from `ctx.Value(ws.SenderKey)`, store senders in shared controller state, copy recipients while locked, then send after releasing the lock.

Spine currently has no application-level connect/disconnect callback. A sender kept by application state may only be noticed as stale on a later failed send. Do not treat an in-memory sender map as durable presence; use an external presence store with expiry for multi-instance or strict presence semantics.

### WebSocket handshake authentication

Authentication before upgrade belongs in one interceptor instance that implements the four `core.Interceptor` methods plus `core.WebSocketHandshakeInterceptor.PreHandshake`. Register that instance with `app.InterceptorFor(boot.InterceptorWebSocket, auth)`. In `PreHandshake`, read headers/query/cookies from `core.WebSocketHandshakeContext` and return a 4xx `httperr` on rejection. Copy the complete constant-time token implementation from the chat demo's [`interceptor/auth_interceptor.go`](https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-simple-chat-demo/blob/b1fe598329eb79828eb4c84903c7fa3847d35914/interceptor/auth_interceptor.go), not a partial interface implementation.

A connection slot is reserved before `PreHandshake`; rejected handshakes release it. `PreHandshake` runs before HTTP upgrade. Message-level `PreHandle` still runs for every accepted message.

Inside a message interceptor, type-assert `core.ExecutionContext` to `core.WebSocketMessageContext` to inspect the immutable handshake headers, query values, cookies, remote address, host, and request URI. These request-view interfaces are not controller handler parameters.

### WebSocket runtime options

WebSocket requires non-nil `HTTP`. Configure `HTTP.WebSocket` fields such as `AllowedOrigins`, `TrustedProxyCIDRs`, `MaxConnections`, `MaxMessageBytes`, `HandshakeTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, and `PingInterval`.

- Empty `AllowedOrigins` performs scheme-and-host same-origin checks when an `Origin` header is present; non-browser clients without `Origin` are allowed.
- Exact production origins are preferred. `*` allows every origin.
- Trusted proxies must remove or overwrite client-supplied forwarding headers.
- Zero limits/timeouts select bounded framework defaults.
- Default active-plus-pending connection capacity is `boot.DefaultWebSocketMaxConnections` (1024).
- Use a positive limit or explicit `boot.UnlimitedWebSocketConnections`.
- Capacity rejection is HTTP 503 with `Retry-After` and code `WEBSOCKET_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`.
- Oversized messages close with WebSocket code 1009.

## Domain events and Kafka

An event must implement:

```go
type DomainEvent interface {
	Name() string
	OccurredAt() time.Time
}
```

Example event:

```go
type OrderCreated struct {
	EventID string    `json:"event_id"`
	OrderID int64     `json:"order_id"`
	At      time.Time `json:"at"`
}

func (e OrderCreated) Name() string         { return "order.created" }
func (e OrderCreated) OccurredAt() time.Time { return e.At }
```

Queue it from an HTTP, WebSocket, or consumer handler's `context.Context`:

```go
publish.Event(ctx, OrderCreated{
	EventID: eventID,
	OrderID: orderID.Value,
	At:      time.Now().UTC(),
})
```

`publish.Event` adds the event to the current execution context. Spine dispatches queued events only after the handler succeeds and, for HTTP, after response preparation succeeds. The function returns no error. If no writer is configured, the handler can still succeed while nothing is delivered externally, so every publishing process must register a platform factory with `Config.Publish: true` deliberately.

Use a consumer signature such as `func (c *OrderConsumer) OnCreated(ctx context.Context, eventName string, event OrderCreated) error`. Register `NewOrderConsumer` with `app.Constructor`, then check the error from `app.Consumers().Register("order.created", (*OrderConsumer).OnCreated)`. Consumer inputs are `context.Context`, event name `string`, raw `[]byte`, and a non-pointer struct decoded from JSON. A topic can have only one registered handler; make it idempotent by stable event ID.

### Kafka configuration

Import `kafkaplatform "github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-kafka-platform"`. Inside BuildApplication:

```go
factory, err := kafkaplatform.NewFactory(kafkaplatform.Config{
    Brokers: []string{"kafka.example.com:9093"},
    Consume: true,
    Publish: true,
    GroupID: "order-service",
    TopicPrefix: "prod.",
})
if err != nil {
    return nil, boot.Options{}, err
}
app := spine.New(echoplatform.Option(), spine.WithEventAdapter("events", factory,
    spine.WithEventConsumerRetry(boot.ConsumerRetryOptions{MaxAttempts: 5}),
    spine.WithEventSettlementTimeout(5 * time.Second),
))
```

Kafka Config owns brokers, roles, GroupID, TopicPrefix, TLS, Dialer, Transport, StartupTimeout, and WriteTimeout. Default TLS is 1.2+. Use AllowInsecureTransport only for isolated local plaintext brokers; explicit TLS conflicts with that option. TopicPrefix maps both publication and subscription names: register `order.created` in the app and provision `prod.order.created` for both factories using `prod.`.

Common ConsumerRetry defaults are 100ms initial delay, 5s maximum delay, multiplier 2, jitter 0.2, and unlimited transport retries with MaxAttempts 0. It controls reader reconstruction, not handler retry budgets. SettlementTimeout defaults to 5s for ACK/NACK. ACK follows handler/post-hook success; failures NACK. Kafka failed-offset protection prevents later commits from skipping a failed record. Poison records can block a partition; automatic DLQ selection is not provided. Prepare checks broker/topic readiness for registered consumer readers, and Run starts those same readers. Kafka publisher-only Prepare/startup is not evidence of a broker connection; verify actual publication separately. A consumer-only process omits HTTP and handles SIGINT/SIGTERM.

### Transactional outbox boundary

`publish.Event` is request-scoped publication, not a database transaction. For durable database-plus-event behavior:

1. Write the business row and outbox row in one database transaction.
2. Give the event a stable unique ID.
3. A separate relay publishes pending rows with broker acknowledgements.
4. Mark the row published after acknowledgement.
5. Accept that a crash between publish and marking can duplicate delivery.
6. Deduplicate in every downstream consumer.

The MSA demo's `scenarios/outbox` illustrates the boundary with a JSON-file store and direct `kafka-go`; it is educational, not a production multi-process database outbox.

## RabbitMQ variant

Use `rabbitmqplatform.NewFactory(rabbitmqplatform.Config{URL: ..., Exchange: ..., Consume: true, Publish: true})`, check the error, and register it with `spine.WithEventAdapter`. Event publication and consumer registration APIs are unchanged.

- AMQPS is required by default. Local AMQP needs explicit AllowInsecureTransport.
- PrefetchCount defaults to 1. FailurePolicy defaults to rabbitmqplatform.FailureReject; FailureRequeue can repeat indefinitely.
- DeadLetter uses rabbitmqplatform.DeadLetter; provision its exchange first.
- TopicPrefix maps published routing keys and subscription bindings; QueuePrefix maps queue names.
- Persistent messages, mandatory routing, and publisher confirms are enabled. OperationTimeout defaults to 5s.
- There is no automatic failed-message republishing via PublisherRetry. Application retries after lost confirmation can duplicate delivery.
- Multiple publish-capable event adapters receive each queued event. Keep consumers idempotent.

## Runtime and security defaults

Zero values select bounded defaults for HTTP timeouts, header size, request body size, WebSocket size/timeouts/capacity, and shutdown timeout. Consumer retry delays are bounded by default, while `MaxAttempts: 0` means unlimited transport retries. RabbitMQ OperationTimeout defaults to 5s and does not add automatic message republishing.

Important exceptions and rules:

- `HTTPOptions.MaxBodyBytes < 0` explicitly disables the request-body limit.
- Spine v0.6.5 with Echo platform v0.1.0 returns HTTP 400 for malformed JSON and invalid path values, and 415 for unsupported body Content-Type. Business rules remain application-owned; optional DTO validation runs only when a validator is selected.
- Request bodies above the configured maximum produce HTTP 413.
- `DisableRecover: false` (the zero value) keeps recovery enabled.
- Use `EnableGracefulShutdown: true` for signal-driven HTTP shutdown.
- Zero `ShutdownTimeout` uses the 10-second framework default; set a deliberate positive value when the application's HTTP/custom-transport drain budget differs.
- `ShutdownTimeout` does not forcibly cap consumer handler/ACK/NACK drain; consumer `Stop` waits for that runtime to finish.
- Do not log broker URLs with embedded credentials or secret tokens.
- Do not trust forwarded headers unless the immediate peer matches an exact configured proxy CIDR.

Read the [security configuration reference](/en/reference/security-configuration) and the latest applicable framework migration guide before changing production defaults.

## External example details

### Bun ORM + Swagger: spine-user-demo

Reviewed snapshot: [`b07d2bb`](https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-user-demo/tree/b07d2bb35d6e0b499c6f6974e1d34f3a4fafffba), Go `1.25.5`, Spine `v0.5.1`.

Follow `HTTP -> controller -> service -> repository -> Bun -> MySQL`. Together, `main.go`, `routes/user_routes.go`, `interceptor/tx_interceptor.go`, `repository/user_repository.go`, and the transaction E2E show DI, `bun.IDB` reuse across `*bun.DB`/`bun.Tx`, response-aware rollback, error mapping, and Swaggo UI. Set `SPINE_DEMO_MYSQL_DSN`, run `go run . -migrate` before the first `go run .`, and open `/swagger/index.html`. Actual CRUD uses `/users?id=1`, not `/users/:id`, with no list endpoint; prefer code over mismatching README/generated fields.

### Kafka MSA: spine-simple-msa-demo

Reviewed snapshot: [`aa3f0fa`](https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-simple-msa-demo/tree/aa3f0fae8057ec0999fadaafc9295b7c7987afbb), Go `1.25.5`, Spine `v0.5.1`.

The repository name ends in `-demo`, but its `go.mod` module/import path is `github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-simple-msa`. Do not rewrite imports to add `-demo`.

The flow is `POST order -> order.created -> stock idempotency decision -> stock.reserved|stock.rejected -> order result consumer -> GET status`. Read both app `main.go` files, `shared/events`, and `scenarios/outbox`; run the stock worker then order HTTP service. Docker E2E uses Redpanda port `19092`, while manual defaults use Kafka `9092`. Topic prefix must include its separator and match both processes. JSON/in-memory stores are educational; production provisioning, keys, retention, schemas, retry topics, and DLQ remain application work.

### WebSocket chat: spine-simple-chat-demo

Reviewed snapshot: [`b1fe598`](https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-simple-chat-demo/tree/b1fe598329eb79828eb4c84903c7fa3847d35914), Go `1.25.5`, Spine `v0.5.1`.

This single-process in-memory server implements authenticated `join -> message -> leave`, one room per connection, room broadcast, typed errors, and runtime limit tests. Read its main, auth interceptor, controller, and E2E. Query `token` or exact `Authorization: Bearer ...` authenticates the handshake; the header wins, and blank config falls back to public `demo-token`, so production must override it and use `wss://`. There is no frontend, persistence, multi-instance state, or user/room authorization. Disconnect cleanup waits for a failed send; 1000-rune logical messages can exceed the 4096-byte frame limit; `leave` keeps the socket open. Build-tagged E2E requires a running server and `go test -tags=e2e -v ./e2e`.

## Agent implementation checklist

- Identify required transports, then read the closest example's actual `main.go`, handler, test, and `go.mod`.
- Define DTO/signature contracts, DI direction, idempotency key, transaction/outbox boundary, retry/DLQ policy, and shutdown behavior before wiring routes.
- Centralize assembly; use semantic inputs, supported outputs, narrow interceptor scopes, and environment-backed secrets.
- Check every registration/startup error; enable `HTTP` only where a listener is intended.
- Verify WebSocket origins/auth/capacity, secure broker transport, poison-message behavior, and durable consumer deduplication.
- Remember that `Validate` does not replace DI warm-up, route-ambiguity checks, or live consumer readiness in `Run`.

For Go changes, format the edited files, then run the CLI gates:

```sh
gofmt -w <changed-go-files>
spine contract check --json
spine verify --json
```

Run `go test -race ./...` separately when the change affects concurrency.

Run relevant broker/database/WebSocket E2E separately. For the historical external MSA demo only, run this PowerShell example from that demo repository root:

```powershell
$env:SPINE_DEMO_KAFKA_BROKER = "localhost:19092"
go run ./stock-app
```
